title: Azure AI Search and Azure AI Inference
description: Use Azure.AI.Search v1 and Azure.AI.Inference with Microsoft.Extensions.AI abstractions for modern .NET RAG backends.

blocks.text: Azure AI Search and Azure AI Inference are the current Microsoft-backed options for retrieval and generation in .NET. Azure.AI.Search v1 replaces the older Azure.Search.Documents namespace, and Azure.AI.Inference provides one client for Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry, and Azure AI Studio inference endpoints.

blocks.title: What changed from v11
items: Namespace moved to Azure.AI.Search with SearchClient and SearchOptions.
Vector search uses VectorizedQuery from Azure.AI.Search.Models.
Indexes, indexers, and skillsets are managed via Azure AI Search management clients or the portal.

blocks.title: Azure.AI.Search client setup
blocks.content: Create a SearchClient with the new Azure.AI.Search v1 namespace.

blocks.text: Azure.AI.Inference unifies calls to Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry, and Azure AI Studio Inference under one client. It works with Microsoft.Extensions.AI so you can keep IChatClient abstractions while targeting Azure endpoints.

blocks.title: Azure AI Inference with Microsoft.Extensions.AI
blocks.content: Use AzureAIChatClient from Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Azure or the lower-level Azure.AI.Inference client.

blocks.title: Prefer abstractions
blocks.text: Use IChatClient and IEmbeddingGenerator from Microsoft.Extensions.AI so you can swap providers without changing business logic. Use Azure.AI.Inference only when you need provider-specific features.

items.text: I can create a SearchClient with Azure.AI.Search v1
items.hint: Use SearchClient from Azure.AI.Search with DefaultAzureCredential

items.text: I can run vector search with VectorizedQuery
I can call Azure AI Inference through Microsoft.Extensions.AI

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: Azure.AI.Search v1 is the current namespace for search operations.
Azure.AI.Inference unifies Azure OpenAI, Foundry, and AI Studio endpoints.
blocks.takeaway: Use Azure.AI.Search v1 and Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Azure for new .NET AI backends on Azure.
